deviations: The pre-registered grid (main and physics slices) runs the registered pairwise 0.8 m guard (separation_rule local), as pre-registered (decision D-126).

The coop_comparison slice (point mass, clean preset, Run D's cooperative reciprocal velocity rule, separation_rule coop, decision D-123) was added after the pre-registration, for comparison only; it is not part of the pre-registered grid.
guard_activations counts pair-steps inside 0.8 m in the local slices; in the coop_comparison slice it counts drone control steps where the coop rule changed the velocity.

hand_check.coop_rule_comparison_note: Same hand formula applied to the coop_comparison slice (separation_rule coop), added after the pre-registration for comparison only.
hand_check.hand_formula: per-axis std = sigma * sqrt(a / (2 - a)), a = 1 - exp(-(1/30)/0.25)

limits: Simulated only: no drone or radio hardware was used.
Link loss patterns are synthetic (named presets in sim/missions/presets.py), never measured.
Vehicle parameters are literature-derived (point mass, or the crazyflie-class physics profile).
Camera fixes, link loss, and vehicle dynamics are synthetic.

separation_rule coop (default): each drone's goal passes through Run D's reciprocal velocity rule (sim.coop.avoidance.safe_velocity) using the delivered camera fixes dead-reckoned with telemetry velocity, radius 0.35 m plus Run D's buffer for the fix latency (runs/d4-separation/buffer.json).  Run D tested it only on kinematic point masses with independent loss; telemetry velocity is the simulated vehicle's own, without estimation noise.  guard_activations counts drone control steps where the rule changed the preferred velocity.
separation_rule local: pairwise 0.8 m goal guard moving a goal 0.4 m away, a stand-in until Run D, kept for comparison; guard_activations counts pair-steps inside 0.8 m.
The downwash value uses the narrow equivalent-disk interaction model and default hover inputs.
In EXP-034 the pre-registered grid uses separation_rule local (the registered 0.8 m guard) and the coop_comparison slice uses separation_rule coop; the mission's own default does not apply here.
notes: min_separation_m is taken over the whole run, including the start from randomly offset positions.

The offboard physics adapter differences the last two position fixes for velocity, a contract design choice. Velocity noise per axis is about sqrt(2) x 30 x sigma at 30 Hz (difference of two fixes 1/30 s apart).
prediction: point mass at zero latency matches the hand formula within 10 %; latency up to 0.2 s raises the error by under 30 % (the first-order loop with delay stays stable below about (pi/2) tau = 0.39 s, but the margin shrinks); physics adapter errors larger than the point mass at the same sigma (PD loop with lower damping passes more noise) and grows faster with latency (Run A: position feedback edge 0.33 s). Separation never near 0.5 m (slots 2 m apart, errors of centimetres).
prediction_source: pre-registered before the runs (EXP-034 section of the private pre-registration)
